source_refs.title: If you can't send or receive messages on your iPhone or iPad - Apple Support
source_refs.section: If you see a red exclamation point
source_refs.applicability: iPhone or iPad; the section gives no iOS version limit
source_refs.model_visible_text: On iPhone: If you see a red exclamation point with an alert that says 'Not Delivered': 1. Check your network connection. 2. Tap the red exclamation point, then tap 'Try Again.' 3. If the message still won't send, tap the red exclamation point, then tap 'Send as Text Message.'
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps copied from the named section; excerpt quoted exactly; the labels Try Again and Send as Text Message confirmed by a narrower exact fetch; the Not Delivered alert name is from a fetch summary; the messaging rates note left out as billing

source_refs.title: Fix problems sending, receiving, or connecting to Google Messages - Android - Google Messages
source_refs.section: Fix problems sending or receiving messages
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Verify that Google Messages is set as your default texting app.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: 1. Make sure you have the most updated version of Google Messages. 2. If you have a SIM card, ensure that it is inserted properly. 3. Verify that Google Messages is set as your default texting app. 4. Check your plan or credit balance to see that you have enough to send/receive messages. 5. See if you have signal. 6. Check if you're on airplane mode. If you are, turn it off.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; steps copied from the named section; the excerpt and the step wording confirmed by exact fetch of the section

source_refs.title: Fix problems sending, receiving, or connecting to Google Messages - Android - Google Messages
source_refs.section: Fix problems sending or receiving messages
source_refs.applicability: Android phones using Google Messages; the RCS line applies when the carrier does not support RCS
source_refs.verified_excerpt: Make sure that your carrier supports SMS, MMS, or RCS messaging.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: 1. Make sure that your carrier supports SMS, MMS, or RCS messaging. If you get the message 'Not supported - RCS chats are not supported by your carrier,' RCS isn't currently supported by your carrier.
source_refs.extraction_method: WebFetch of the official page on 2026-11-17; the step and the RCS message text confirmed by exact fetch; the RCS message label is quoted from the page with single quotes

source_refs.title: Fix problems sending, receiving, or connecting to Google Messages - Android - Google Messages
source_refs.section: Fix problems sending or receiving messages
source_refs.applicability: Android phones using Google Messages; each line applies only in the situation it names
source_refs.verified_excerpt: If you're switching from an iPhone, make sure you've deactivated iMessage for your number.
source_refs.model_visible_text: On Android: If you're on Fi, sign in to the Project Fi app. If you're switching from an iPhone, make sure you've deactivated iMessage for your number. If you change messaging apps on your phone and don't receive messages, you may need to turn off RCS chats.
